stories.label: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms over West Bank settlements
stories.summary: Britain froze the assets of eight Israeli construction companies that build settlements in the occupied West Bank, and of a settler group that blocks aid trucks into Gaza. Lead with who is named — the firms (Har Hevron among them) and the aid-blocking group — and the mechanism: London is now sanctioning the companies that pour the concrete, not only violent individual settlers. Say what the freeze does and does not reach (UK assets, UK business), and that it lands while Palestinians in Gaza still depend on the aid these groups obstruct. Datelined London.

stories.label: Tamil Nadu Issues Urgent Alert As Cyclonic Storm Akvan Approaches
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan, the third storm to form in the Bay of Bengal in under a month after Arnab and Murasu, is forecast by the India Meteorological Department to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast near Nellore on November 20, with Tamil Nadu and Odisha on alert. Lead with the landfall date and place, the winds (GDACS Orange, up to 93 km/h) and who must move: coastal fishing communities and the districts under evacuation orders. The structural point is three storms in four weeks hitting the same coast before it has recovered. Datelined Nellore.

stories.label: Companies That Helped Gut EU Climate Law Turn Up for COP31
stories.summary: Members of the 'Competitiveness Roundtable', a secretive coalition of fossil-fuel and heavy-industry companies that lobbied to strip down EU climate law, turned up in force at COP31 while the US government boycotted the talks. Lead with the names of the companies and what each lobbied to weaken in Brussels, then the accountability gap: the firms that watered down the rules now sit inside the room where the next ones are negotiated. Follows our COP31 AI-pledge story, where only nine countries signed. Datelined Antalya.

stories.label: Germany, UK push back after US criticizes Ukraine's deep strikes into Russia
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official questioned whether Ukraine's long-range strikes inside Russia work and warned they harden Russian resolve; Germany and Britain publicly rejected that on November 17. The new development is the open split among Ukraine's backers, days after the Kerch bridge span fell to exactly those strikes. Lead with who said what in Brussels, and the stake: whether Washington's doubts translate into limits on weapons or targeting data that Berlin and London cannot replace. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: US Fed's Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House hearing
stories.summary: Fed Governor Lisa Cook, whom Trump has tried to fire since August 2025, told a White House committee through her lawyers that she will not appear at next month's hearing on her removal, calling the process unfair. Lead with the refusal and the mechanism: a president building an in-house tribunal to remove a central-bank governor is a test of whether Fed independence survives, and with it who sets the price of money worldwide. Chart the Fed funds rate and the US 10-year Treasury yield. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Bacolod anti-Pax Silica protest raises alarm over proposed copper mine
stories.summary: A youth-led protest in Bacolod against Pax Silica, the US initiative to lock in supplies of critical minerals and chip technology, turned on a proposed copper mine in Hinoba-an, southern Negros Occidental. Lead with the mine: who holds the permit, how much land and water it takes, and the communities downstream. The mechanism: Washington's push to move mineral supply away from China lands as a mine in a Philippine province, days after the Quad met in Manila on mineral dependence. Datelined Bacolod.

stories.label: 6倍超额认购，Anthropic IPO发行价或再上调！
stories.summary: The new development since our retail-exposure story: Anthropic's IPO book is at least six times oversubscribed (The Information, via Zhidx), so the price could rise from $70–78 to $83–85 a share and the valuation to about $1.5 trillion, pricing due November 19. Lead with the size: 825 million shares, roughly $68–70 billion raised, with Google and Nvidia each putting $10 billion into a parallel placement and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft and TSMC also buying in. The structural point is that the chipmakers and clouds that sell to Anthropic are also its shareholders. Datelined New York.

stories.label: Waymo temporarily pulls driverless taxis from all US freeways
stories.summary: California's DMV banned Waymo's driverless taxis from state freeways after a series of traffic incidents, and Waymo then pulled them off freeways in every US state. Lead with the regulator acting first and the company extending the retreat nationwide, and name the incidents that triggered it. The mechanism: high-speed driving is where a robotaxi's errors are least forgiving, and a state licensing agency, not federal safety law, set the limit. Datelined San Francisco.

stories.label: Huawei’s new sub-brand OSTA set to launch first phone, reportedly featuring Kirin 9030S chip
stories.summary: Huawei's new AI-phone sub-brand OSTA (Xingmang) debuts on November 20, its first handset reportedly running the Kirin 9030S, a chip made in China under US export controls. Lead with the chip: what is known of its process node and who fabs it, and what it says about how far Chinese chipmaking has come despite the ASML equipment bans. Then the strategy: a separate AI-first brand lets Huawei widen its lineup at home. Datelined Shenzhen.

stories.label: AI伴侣的孤独陷阱
stories.summary: A Stanford study of 460,000 real chat logs with AI companions found that for people with weak social networks, the companionship did not relieve loneliness — it deepened it. Lead with that finding and the sample size, and name the study's authors and the measure of loneliness. The mechanism: an always-available companion displaces the human contact the lonely most lack, and the business model rewards more engagement. Datelined Stanford.

stories.label: Nvidia forecasts $130 billion revenue for Q4, beating estimates amid leadership crisis after Jensen Huang's exit
stories.summary: The first results since Jensen Huang resigned: $65.3 billion in Q3 profit and a $130 billion Q4 forecast, presented by interim CEO Colette Kress. Lead with the numbers against the crisis: demand for AI chips has not flinched while the founder is gone, a spy inquiry hangs over the company and the new US rule on overseas data centers threatens its China-linked revenue. New development on the Huang arc: the earnings and the first call without him.

stories.label: Why are there so many huge outages right now? Some possible causes
stories.summary: New development past the NSA and United outages already covered: on Tuesday Gmail, Apple Pay and iCloud also went down, and Trump downplayed the run. Lead with the pattern, not one outage: email for many US companies, thousands of grounded flights and a classified network in days. The mechanism to test is whether cuts to tech staff in government and companies removed the people who kept these systems up. Say plainly that no cause has been established.

stories.label: GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol
stories.summary: OpenAI released two GPT-6.2 models, Astra and Sol (907 points and 547 comments on Hacker News). Lead with what the split between the two models is for and the concrete benchmark, price or capability numbers OpenAI publishes, and say which claims are OpenAI's own. The reader is a developer choosing which model to build on.

stories.label: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water
stories.summary: Harvard chemists used molecules designed for flow batteries to drive reactions used in making medicines with electricity, at the boundary where oil and water meet, instead of heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hydrogen gas. Lead with what it replaces and the yield or efficiency figure the team reports. Name the journal.

stories.label: France is not 'co-belligerent' in Ukraine, French minister says
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot confirmed French military personnel are in Ukraine, calling it a training and technical-support mission, and denied that this makes France a party to the war. Lead with the admission of the presence. The mechanism is the legal line of co-belligerence, which Moscow has said would make such personnel targets. Attribute Russia's reaction to TASS, a Russian state news agency.

stories.label: CCTV captures Russian military plane crash in Siberia that killed all 19 onboard
stories.summary: An An-12 military transport crashed near Yagunovo in Kemerovo region, killing all 19 aboard, according to Russia's Defence Ministry. Lead with the toll and the aircraft's age: the An-12 is a Soviet design from the 1950s still carrying Russia's wartime military logistics. Report the cause only as officials state it.

stories.label: He resisted Israeli occupation in Palestine. Italy is imprisoning him for it.
stories.summary: An Italian court is holding a Palestinian on terrorism charges for armed resistance to the Israeli occupation in the West Bank, acts committed outside Italy against an occupying army. Lead with the person, the charge and the sentence or stage of the case. The precedent: a European court applying its own terrorism law to resistance that international law treats differently, partly on evidence from Israel.

stories.label: Who’s Behind the Poll Claiming Cubans Would Support a U.S. Invasion?
stories.summary: A poll circulating in Washington says most Cubans would not oppose a US military intervention, and Drop Site traces the groups behind it to millions in US government funding. Lead with the funding trail and its amounts. The mechanism is a state-funded poll used to justify a war against the country it surveyed. Dateline it in Havana, where the policy lands.

stories.label: Akwa Ibom fishing communities to petition oil regulators, National Assembly over recurring pollution
stories.summary: Every rainy season an oil sheen covers the fishing waters of Ntan Mbat in Akwa Ibom, and residents trace it to decades-old capped wells. They will petition petroleum regulators and the National Assembly. Lead with the livelihoods lost. The accountability gap: abandoned wells whose operator and decommissioning duty nobody enforces, a pattern across the Niger Delta.

stories.label: Copper mine using ‘lawfare’ against Colombia environmental activists: NGO report
stories.summary: An NGO report finds that communities opposing a Canadian-owned copper project in the Colombian Amazon face lawsuits and criminal complaints meant to silence them. Lead with the number and kind of legal actions and who filed them. The mechanism: as copper demand for electrification grows, the conflict moves from the mine site into the courts. Name copper.

stories.label: Documentos do Deutsche Bank ligam empresas de Trump a esquemas de lavagem de dinheiro
stories.summary: New development from the Deutsche Bank leak already covered: internal documents show the bank held evidence linking companies of the sitting US president to money-laundering schemes and Russia. Lead with the specific companies, transactions and amounts, and what the bank did or did not do with what it knew. The accountability point is the compliance failure of a global bank. Dateline Frankfurt.

stories.label: Las millonarias adendas con Etesa que beneficiaron a Iverco, Neminca y Carretero
stories.summary: Through addenda, three contracts that Etesa, the state power-transmission company, signed with Iverco and Neminca grew from $231.9 million to $426.8 million, an 84% increase. Contracorriente ties the firms to Carretero, Líctor Reyna and Ewaldo Pitti. Lead with the near-doubling. The mechanism is contract amendment as a way to move public money without a new tender, paid for by electricity users.

stories.label: Malaysia-Taiwan: Anwar’s China line triggers a quiet investment freeze
stories.summary: Taiwan has quietly frozen investment in Malaysia in response to Anwar Ibrahim's alignment with Beijing, while Taiwanese firms' own stake in Malaysian chip and electronics plants limits how hard Taipei can push. Lead with the size of Taiwanese investment at stake and the projects paused. The mechanism: a Muslim-majority middle power whose factories depend on both sides of the Taiwan Strait.

stories.label: Is Iran plotting a 'dirty bomb' attack in the US? What we know
stories.summary: Trump said in Manila that a reported Iranian plot to detonate a radiological 'dirty bomb' in Washington is being taken 'very seriously', all but confirming a CNN report that US spy agencies believe Tehran may already have smuggled nuclear material into the country. Lead with what is claimed versus what is shown: the claim rests on unnamed intelligence officials, no material has been publicly found, and it lands while a third US carrier sits in the Gulf and a ceasefire is fraying. Explain what a dirty bomb is (radiological dispersal, not a nuclear detonation) and how such an intelligence claim can serve as a pretext for escalation.

stories.label: Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks
stories.summary: New since the Kerch bridge coverage: Russia answered with another large overnight attack on Ukrainian cities that damaged two key facilities, a Ukrainian drone strike killed two people in Crimea, and Germany and Norway announced a joint air-defence package for Kyiv. Lead with the civilians on both sides of the strike exchange, counted equally, then the mechanism: each side is now targeting the other's logistics arteries (bridge, power grid), and Europe, not Washington, is paying for the interceptors.

stories.label: At least nine killed, 13 wounded in Saudi-led coalition attacks on Yemen
stories.summary: Saudi-led coalition strikes on Hodeidah and Saada governorates killed at least nine and wounded 13, according to Houthi health authorities as relayed by Russian state agency TASS; one strike hit a foam-rubber factory in northern Hodeidah. Attribute the toll throughout (only state media in the feed). Lead with the dead and the civilian target, then the context: this follows Houthi missiles on Riyadh's King Khalid airport and the Yemeni government's withdrawal from Bab el-Mandeb, so the coalition's air war is resuming on the Red Sea coast.

stories.label: Joy, anticipation as student movement enters Serbia's new parliament
stories.summary: Serbia's new parliament sat for the first time with the Student List, a grassroots movement born of the anti-corruption protests, as a major bloc after the October 25 vote upended Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party. Lead with the seat count and what it changes for who can form a government, then the mechanism: a protest movement with no party machine turning street pressure into votes, and what it can and cannot block from opposition.

stories.label: What Happens to Western Sahara After the UN Mission Ends?
stories.summary: The UN Security Council failed to renew MINURSO, ending a 35-year peacekeeping mission and with it the UN's last formal commitment to a self-determination referendum for the Sahrawi people. Lead with what disappears: the ceasefire monitors between Morocco and the Polisario Front and the referendum mandate. Then who gains (Morocco's autonomy plan, backed by the US and France) and who loses (Sahrawis in the Tindouf camps in Algeria), and the risk of renewed fighting along the berm.

stories.label: Street medicine vendors are dangerously filling Haiti’s healthcare gaps
stories.summary: With gangs controlling much of Port-au-Prince and hospitals closed or unreachable, Haitians buy medicines from untrained street vendors who sell drugs of unknown origin stored in heat and sun. Lead with the risk to patients (wrong doses, counterfeit or degraded antibiotics), then the mechanism: state collapse pushes primary care onto an unregulated market, and who is accountable for the absent health system.

stories.label: Rs24bn additional QTA proposed by Discos draws protest from industrial consumers
stories.summary: Pakistan's state power distribution companies asked NEPRA for a Rs24 billion quarterly tariff adjustment, driven by capacity payments to idle power plants, O&M costs and system losses, and industrial consumers protested at the hearing. Lead with who pays: industry and households cover the cost of plants paid whether or not they generate, and of theft and line losses the Discos fail to stop. Tie it to the IMF/ADB reform conditions Pakistan is under.

stories.label: Hong Kong, Swift explore tokenized deposits to bring 24/7 speed to bank payments
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Swift are testing tokenized deposits with major banks: blockchain-based bank money that settles around the clock while staying a bank liability. Lead with the mechanism and why banks want it: it lets them match stablecoin speed without losing deposits to stablecoin issuers. Note the geopolitics: Hong Kong positioning as the bridge for offshore yuan and cross-border settlement.

stories.label: 刚刚，诺奖得主的AI公司融了333亿
stories.summary: Isomorphic Labs, the London AI drug-design company founded by Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis, raised $5 billion in a Series C led by Greenoaks and Sequoia, likely the largest single round in AI drug discovery, bringing disclosed funding to $7.7 billion. Lead with the gap: every result so far is preclinical, no drug has entered human trials. Note the investors include Abu Dhabi's MGX, Singapore's Temasek and the UK sovereign AI fund. Reported here by Chinese tech outlet Zhidx.

stories.label: OpenAI Shut Down Sora. Kuaishou Is Betting Bigger on Kling.
stories.summary: OpenAI shut down its Sora video generator, while Kuaishou is doubling down on Kling and preparing a Hong Kong listing for it. Lead with the reversal: the Chinese short-video company kept investing where the US leader retreated. The mechanism: Kuaishou monetises video generation through its own creator platform and paying users, while standalone generation burns compute without a business behind it.

stories.label: The Department of Justice Is Using AI Detector Pangram Against Defense Attorneys
stories.summary: US federal prosecutors are running defence filings through the AI-text detector Pangram and citing the scores in court to attack defence attorneys ('this case has turned into defense by ChatGPT'). Lead with the precedent: a probabilistic classifier with known false positives becomes evidence against a defendant's counsel. Explain how such detectors work and why their error rates matter when the state holds the tool.

stories.label: US Electronic Spy Agency Suffers Outage of Classified Network
stories.summary: NSA Net, the National Security Agency's classified internal network, has been down since at least early Tuesday, sending some staff home. Lead with the fact itself and what is not known (cause, cyberattack or failure). Then the pattern: it follows a week of outages at Chase, United Airlines and the FAA, and comes amid an Iran conflict in which a cyber-attack would be a plausible line of inquiry; state what is and is not confirmed.

stories.label: Proposed GDPR changes: Workplace Data Abuses Could Soon Be Harder to Uncover
stories.summary: A European Trade Union Institute study finds the European Commission's Digital Omnibus, proposed without a full impact assessment, would weaken GDPR data-access rights that workers use to expose algorithmic management. Lead with the case that proves the stakes: Uber drivers used data access requests to win back pay and contest automated firings. Name what the Omnibus changes and who gains (platform employers).

stories.label: Lakes Are Bizarrely Syncing Up Globally, And Scientists Are Worried
stories.summary: A satellite study finds lakes worldwide are increasingly synchronised in their behaviour, a 'genuine, global-scale phenomenon'. Lead with the finding and the number from the paper, then the mechanism: when distant lakes respond together, a shared driver such as climate warming is overriding local conditions, and synchronised stress means droughts or blooms hit many water supplies at once rather than being buffered.

stories.label: Iran claims strike on Bahrain air base as tensions persist
stories.summary: The IRGC says it sent drones at a US radar system at Isa air base in Bahrain; Bahraini state TV says the attack was thwarted. Lead with the target: Iran is now striking US military assets on Gulf soil, not only shipping, which puts the host state and its people in the line of fire. Attribute each side's claims (IRGC, Bahrain state TV; TASS is state media). Context: a Polymarket contract on a US-Iran ceasefire by 22 November rose from 53% to 68% this week, yet strikes continue. Datelined Manama.

stories.label: Russia’s Kerch Bridge Road Vehicle Span Has Been Destroyed By Ukraine
stories.summary: This is a material new development on the 11-16 story: a second strike in under 24 hours dropped a road span of the Kerch Strait Bridge, and post-dawn imagery confirms it. Lead with the dropped span and what it cuts: the road link that supplies occupied Crimea, which now depends on the rail deck and ferries. Mention timing: this comes while Washington is pressing Kyiv to cede Donbas. Attribute imagery-based claims to TWZ. Datelined Kerch.

stories.label: One Repost, Three Years in Prison: Why Was a Kloop Reader Convicted?
stories.summary: For the first time in Kyrgyzstan, a court has jailed a reader, Baktybek Moldaliev (three years), for reposting a video by an outlet a court had declared 'extremist'. The precedent: an extremism label on a newsroom now makes its audience criminally liable, not just its journalists. Name the court and the law. Kloop is itself the banned outlet, so say so. Datelined Bishkek.

stories.label: Russia-Ukraine war 'very close' to being resolved: Trump
stories.summary: At his first Quad meeting, held in Manila beside the ASEAN summit, Trump says the four nations agreed critical-mineral deals (Nikkei). Lead with the minerals pact, an effort to route supply around China, and say who supplies the ore and who gets the processing. Trump's claim that the Ukraine war is 'very close' to being resolved is secondary and unsupported, so attribute it. Datelined Manila.

stories.label: Autopsy reveals multiple injuries on teenage domestic worker found dead at FIA official's residence in Islamabad
stories.summary: A 13-year-old domestic worker found dead at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency officer was repeatedly assaulted, according to her autopsy. Lead with the autopsy findings and the FIR. The accountability question is whether a state investigator's household will be investigated by the state. Explain how child domestic labour in Pakistan continues despite the law that bans it, and point to earlier cases of the same kind. Datelined Islamabad.

stories.label: De Cos on Path to ECB as Berlin Backs Brunnermeier for Lane Job
stories.summary: A coalition deal in Berlin clears Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos for the ECB presidency. In exchange, Germany nominates Princeton's Markus Brunnermeier for chief economist, the seat that writes the rate proposals. Lead with the trade: Europe's top monetary posts are allocated by national bargaining, not by open competition. Explain what each man's record suggests for the ECB interest rate and the euro.

stories.label: Russia Exports Most Crude Since July as Drones Hammer Refineries
stories.summary: The perverse mechanism: Ukrainian drones knock out Russian refineries, so producers redirect the crude to export terminals, and seaborne exports reach their highest since July. Kyiv's campaign squeezes Russia's domestic fuel supply but adds crude to world markets. Deputy PM Novak, via TASS (state media, attribute), calls restoring the refineries the priority and wants fuel imports to continue. Name the series: Brent crude. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: ETFs, Swaps, Perps Offer Back Door to Anthropic 'Stock' Pre-IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic is seeking up to $90 billion in what may be the biggest IPO ever, with a Nasdaq listing due this week. Retail traders are already buying exposure through ETFs, closed-end funds, swaps and crypto perpetual futures that track a share that does not yet trade. Lead with those instruments and who carries the risk: retail buyers paying premiums on synthetic claims that have no underlying asset. Use Asianet's post-IPO record for SpaceX and Arm. Datelined New York.

stories.label: How Atiku will make crude available for petrol subsidy - Aide
stories.summary: Atiku Abubakar's campaign says he would review Nigeria's crude-supply commitments, including oil pledged against loans, to sell crude to domestic refineries at subsidised rates. Lead with the mechanism: much of Nigeria's output is already committed to repay crude-backed borrowing, which is why cheap petrol depends on unwinding debt deals. Say who pays, whether that is lenders, the treasury or motorists. It is a campaign pledge, so attribute it and set it against the 2023 subsidy removal. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: Optimizely hack turns world's biggest websites into malware dispensers
stories.summary: Attackers broke into Optimizely, an A/B-testing script embedded on major sites, and for a day the BBC, Zoom, HSBC, GitLab and others served malware aimed at visitors' crypto wallets, card details and iPhones. Lead with the supply-chain mechanism: one third-party script tag gives its vendor write access to every page it runs on. Readers who visited those sites on Monday are the ones affected.

stories.label: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI's environmental footprint | New Scientist
stories.summary: Turkey, the COP31 co-host, put forward a pledge to rein in emissions from the AI build-out, and only nine countries signed. Lead with the number and name the signatories and the large data-centre countries that stayed out. The mechanism: the energy and water demand of AI data centres falls under no climate commitment. Datelined Antalya.

stories.label: ETH news: Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade risks breaking up to 15,000 automated apps
stories.summary: An Ethereum Foundation developer warns that the planned Glamsterdam upgrade could break up to 15,000 deployed smart contracts. Compatibility problems have already stalled testing on the Hoodi testnet, and the upgrade has no release date. Lead with the bind: contracts are immutable, so a protocol change can strand the money they hold, and the developers have to choose between progress and backward compatibility.

stories.label: Team extends a qubit's lifetime, correcting errors without measuring them
stories.summary: Researchers extended a qubit's lifetime by correcting its errors without measuring it. Measurement normally collapses quantum states and slows error correction. Lead with the lifetime gain and name the team and the journal. Explain why measurement-free correction matters for building useful quantum computers, and say plainly how far this is from a working machine.

stories.label: Deutsche Bank shares drop after reports on mass data leak
stories.summary: More than 15 million leaked Deutsche Bank files, reviewed by an international media consortium, detail years of failures in risk management, compliance and governance, including $582 million in suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein (per the Financial Times). Lead with the scale of the leak and the compliance failures it documents, not the share drop; name who the bank served and which supervisors missed it. Note Dawn's coverage for the Pakistani angle and that Agência Pública was a consortium partner.

stories.label: Mongolia's president will resign after facing corruption accusations
stories.summary: President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh says he will step down so the investigation the opposition Democratic Party demanded can proceed. Lead with the precedent: a sitting head of state resigning to face a corruption probe. Explain what he is accused of, who decides what happens next under Mongolia's constitution, and how mining money has shaped the country's corruption scandals. Reuters is the independent source; TRT World is Turkish state media.

stories.label: 2 suspected Russian aircraft violate Japan airspace
stories.summary: Japan scrambled fighters and protested after two suspected Russian aircraft entered its airspace on Tuesday, while South Korea scrambled jets and Taiwan responded to Russian aircraft in their air defence zones, all on the day Trump began his Asia trip in Manila. Lead with the three-government response to one flight. Explain the difference between violating sovereign airspace and entering an ADIZ, and what Moscow signals by probing three US partners at once. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: Turkish households buckle under gold price slide, funds crisis
stories.summary: Ordinary Turks hold much of their savings in gold as a hedge against inflation and the lira. Gold's slide to a one-year low, together with a crisis in the investment-fund industry, is reversing the wealth effect that kept household spending up. Lead with who loses: savers who fled the lira into gold. Explain how the slowdown in domestic demand reaches the economy. This continues our 11-16 gold story with the Turkish consequence. Chart gold and the Turkish lira.

stories.label: US details ongoing criminal probe into Nvidia customer Megaspeed
stories.summary: The US Commerce and Justice departments disclosed a two-year criminal investigation into Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company that is Nvidia's Asia-Pacific partner, over the possible diversion of AI chips to China. Lead with the mechanism: how a cloud reseller in a third country can route export-controlled chips around the rules. Tie it to last week's US rule closing the remote-access loophole and the dispute over Jensen Huang's position at Nvidia, which is a new development on that arc. Dateline Singapore.

stories.label: Iraq resumes crude oil pumping for export purposes via pipeline to Turkey, oil minister says
stories.summary: Iraq has restarted exports through the Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline to Turkey at 120,000 barrels a day and plans to raise flows to 500,000. With tankers being mined in the Strait of Hormuz, this is Iraq's one export route that avoids the Gulf. Lead with that: what share of Iraq's exports it can carry and what it means for Baghdad's budget and for Erbil. Chart Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Asian Development Bank approves $500m loan to support Pakistan's federal pension reforms
stories.summary: The ADB approved a $500 million loan tied to reform of Pakistan's federal pensions, whose bill grows faster than the budget can carry. Lead with who pays: name the changes the loan's conditions require (contributory schemes for new hires, indexation, retirement age) and which civil servants and retirees they hit. Explain why lenders are now writing pension terms into Pakistan's fiscal policy alongside the IMF programme. This is separate from the ADB's Karachi BRT conditions.

stories.label: Bilkis Bano: Gujarat riots gang-rape survivor 'heartbroken' after Supreme Court bail for two convicts
stories.summary: India's Supreme Court has granted bail to two of the men serving life sentences for gang-raping Bilkis Bano and murdering 14 members of her family during the 2002 Gujarat riots. The same court reversed their early release in 2024. Lead with her statement of 'pain, shock and disbelief' and the legal history: remission in 2022, garlanded on release, sent back to jail, and now on bail. The accountability question is how a case that set a precedent against impunity is unwinding. Dateline New Delhi.

stories.label: In win against impunity, Indonesian court orders the reform of Military Justice Law
stories.summary: Indonesia's Constitutional Court has ordered reform of the Military Justice Law, under which soldiers accused of crimes against civilians are tried in military courts that rarely convict. Lead with the precedent: once the law is reformed, soldiers who abuse civilians, as in Papua, may face civilian courts. Name who brought the petition, the cases behind it, and the deadline the court set for parliament, which is pushing to expand the military's civilian roles. Dateline Jakarta.

stories.label: Revealed: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia are largest CO2 exporters of all time
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis counts the CO2 embodied in the fossil fuels countries have exported over history, and finds Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia, which co-presides over COP31, are the largest exporters of all time. Lead with the method: territorial accounting charges emissions to the country that burns the fuel, while this one charges the country that extracts and sells it. Explain who that reassigns responsibility to while COP31 negotiators argue over fossil-fuel language.

stories.label: After death in gene therapy trial for a brain disease, progress is reported
stories.summary: Capsida scientists presented their investigation into a patient's death last year in a trial of a brain gene therapy, a death that unsettled the whole field of treatments for brain disease delivered by viral vectors. Lead with what they found killed the patient and the proposed fix: a better way to test the risk in monkeys before treating humans. Explain why the animal models missed it and what that means for other brain gene therapies in trials.

stories.label: ICEYE Launches €2.05B Takeover Bid for Italian Rocket Builder Avio
stories.summary: Finnish radar-satellite operator ICEYE has bid €2.05 billion for Avio, the Italian builder of the Vega rocket, and pledged another €1 billion of investment in Italy, pitching the deal as a 'European sovereign space and defense champion'. Lead with what changes: a satellite company buying its own launcher while Europe is trying to stop depending on SpaceX and Starshield. Explain what the Italian state, which has a stake in Avio and a golden-power veto, must decide. Dateline Rome.

stories.label: Hackers behind record Binance breach move $63 million in ether following DOJ seizures
stories.summary: The hackers behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft, the largest on record, moved nearly $63 million in ether to three new wallets after two weeks of silence that followed US Justice Department seizures. Lead with the mechanism: how stolen crypto is traced on-chain and why seizures recover only part of it. Say who the attackers are believed to be, how much has been frozen, and who absorbs the loss. Do not imply a sale; the wallets are not linked to an exchange.

stories.label: Paraguay's ousted president moved to military prison after reports of gym and suite in custody
stories.summary: A judge ordered former president Santiago Peña, toppled this month over the collapse of a major digital lender, moved to a military prison after reports he was held in a suite with a private gym. Lead with the transfer and what it says about whether accountability reaches the top; explain the mechanism briefly: how a digital lender's implosion brought down a government and who lost their savings. Datelined Asunción.

stories.label: 3 US Aircraft Carriers Operating In Middle East
stories.summary: A third US carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, has arrived in the Gulf, CENTCOM said, while Trump alternates between strike threats on Iran and saying the war is 'effectively over'. Lead with the build-up and the contradiction: three carriers is a posture for escalation, not a wind-down, at the moment prediction markets price a US-Iran ceasefire by 22 November at 68% and an end to the blockade by year-end at 19%. Note the CNN report of Iranian dirty-bomb plotting that the White House says poses 'no credible threat'. Dateline the Gulf, not Washington.

stories.label: Oil tanker burns in Strait of Hormuz after hitting mine
stories.summary: Material new development on the Hormuz arc: a fourth tanker in about a day struck a mine east of the strait and burned, per Iran's army (attribute to Mehr, state media), and Al Jazeera reports a drone alarm at an Iraqi gas field the same night, widening the threat from shipping to Gulf energy infrastructure. Lead with the count and the spread to Iraq; name who pays: shipowners, insurers, and importers of Gulf crude. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Write it as the latest turn of the running mine campaign, not as an isolated incident.

stories.label: Grand Ayatollah Vahid Khorasani passes away
stories.summary: Grand Ayatollah Hossein Vahid Khorasani, one of the oldest and most senior marja' of Shia Islam and a leading teacher at the Qom seminary, has died, his office said (reported by Mehr, state media). Lead with who he was in the hierarchy of religious authority and why it matters in wartime Iran: a senior Qom voice outside the state, and what his death means for the balance of clerical authority. Keep it factual, no hagiography. Datelined Qom.

stories.label: Iran condemns Bahrain's life sentences for scholars
stories.summary: A Bahraini court has handed life sentences and asset confiscation to a group of religious scholars and citizens. Lead with the sentences themselves (who, how many, on what charges) and the pattern of Bahrain's prosecution of its Shia clergy, not with Tehran's condemnation; Iran's reaction is a secondary paragraph. Only source is Mehr (state media): attribute every claim. Datelined Manama.

stories.label: SPECIAL REPORT: Kano's CNG buses remain off roads seven months after launch
stories.summary: Kano State's compressed-natural-gas buses, launched to cut transport costs after fuel-subsidy removal, are still parked seven months later. Lead with the commuter's cost: a pregnant woman paying ₦1,100 to reach hospital. Explain the mechanism (missing CNG refuelling infrastructure, who bought the buses and with what money) and hold the state accountable for a launch without the supply chain. Datelined Kano.

stories.label: ADB attaches strings to continued funding for BRT Red Line project
stories.summary: The Asian Development Bank has attached conditions to its latest extension of financing for Karachi's long-delayed Bus Rapid Transit Red Line. Lead with what the lender now demands and the deadline, then the cost of delay: years of dug-up roads on one of Karachi's main corridors, overruns, and a loan Pakistan repays whether or not the buses run. A case of how multilateral lenders discipline provincial projects. Datelined Karachi.

stories.label: Ezekwesili questions INEC's credibility, demands independent investigation of voter register
stories.summary: Suspected AI-generated photographs have been found in the voters' register of Nigeria's electoral commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections, and former minister Oby Ezekwesili demands an independent investigation by the National Assembly. Lead with the AI-generated photos: how synthetic faces get into a biometric register, how many entries are suspected, and what that means for verification of Africa's largest electorate. Datelined Abuja.

stories.label: “学霸”自首AI作弊，韩国高考紧急布防
stories.summary: South Korea goes into Thursday's college entrance exam (suneung) on alert for AI cheating after a top student confessed to using AI, and after a cheating scandal on the tax-accountant exam; Bloomberg adds the state's usual measures, grounding all flights for 35 minutes and delaying the stock market open. Lead with the new threat, AI via smart glasses and phones, and what proctors are doing against it, then the scale of a state that halts aviation for one exam. Datelined Seoul.

stories.label: United Halts Flights as It Addresses 'Widespread System Outage'
stories.summary: United Airlines grounded flights nationwide over a 'widespread system outage', days after an FAA ground stop and in the same week as repeated outages at major US banks. Lead with the pattern: critical US systems failing one after another ahead of Thanksgiving, and what is known of the cause; do not speculate beyond the reporting. Name the single points of failure. Datelined Chicago.
